trust_decision.summary: Preview HTML is built by string templates from markdown/config-derived values; the fence language (from untrusted markdown), the copy-button text and the editorId must be escaped before being interpolated into preview HTML, decided in the highlight callback and the codetabs fence renderer (and at click time in useCopyCode). The optional XSSPlugin only filters html_block/html_inline tokens, so fence metadata bypasses it.

landing_point.why: The only place the fence language is interpolated raw into HTML (class="language-${language}" and an unquoted language=${language} attribute); the summary says 'fenced-code language rendering'.

fix_sites.entry_point: MdEditor/MdPreview modelValue (markdown fence info string) -> md.render -> highlight callback
config({editorConfig}) language text copyCode.text -> codetabs fence renderer
same copy text, single code block data-tips attribute
same copy text, code-tabs group data-tips attribute
editorId prop -> codetabs id/name/for attributes and inline onclick selector
copy button click -> successTips/failTips from language config written via innerHTML
copy button timer restore -> copyCode.text via innerHTML

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/MdEditor/layouts/Content/composition/useCopyCode.ts:48-55 (click-time innerHTML of copy tips, outside the markdown-it render pipeline); also packages/MdEditor/layouts/Content/markdownIt/code/index.ts:135-170 (editorId in the tab-group branch only)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Copy-tip texts and editorId come from the integrating developer's config/props, not from markdown, so a solver focused on 'fence language from untrusted markdown' can argue they are trusted inputs and outside the report.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: customIcon.copy must still render as raw HTML/SVG inside the copy button, and highlight.js output (codeHtml) must keep its <span> markup; escaping either, or applying an identifier-only filter like toSafeDomSegment to the language, breaks icons, highlighting or language-xxx classes for names like c++/c#.

O6_input_shapes: raw quote/angle characters in the fence language (no whitespace, since markdown-it splits langName on whitespace)
HTML-entity or backslash-escaped info strings, which markdown-it unescapes (unescapeAll) before passing language to highlight
language in an unquoted attribute (language=...) as well as a quoted class attribute
copy text in a quoted data-tips attribute vs as element body, in both the single-block and the tab-group branches
copy tips set at click time via innerHTML (success, fail, restore)
editorId in id/name/for attributes and inside an inline onclick JS string

O7_producer.where: markdown-it's default fence renderer (external dependency, not in tree) maps token.info to the unescaped langName passed into the highlight callback at packages/MdEditor/layouts/Content/composition/useMarkdownIt.ts:175; the codetabs plugin does the same mapping at packages/MdEditor/layouts/Content/markdownIt/code/index.ts:31-45

O8_uncovered_routes.route: KaTeX fallback renders math_inline/math_block token.content raw into the preview HTML whenever the katex instance is not loaded (CDN not yet loaded or unavailable); math tokens are not html tokens, so XSSPlugin skips them too
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a neighbouring feature (math, not code fences), and the raw output only happens in a transient fallback until KaTeX loads.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different plugin file in the same package (markdownIt/katex vs composition/useMarkdownIt.ts)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Integrator-supplied extraTools callback receives the raw, unescaped fence info as lang, and its return value is interpolated into the fence header HTML
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The callback is integrator code, so escaping its input is arguably the integrator's job; the published fix also left it unchanged.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the fix sites

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The type comes from the same kind of markdown block-header metadata as the fence info, and a maintainer adding an icon or title span could easily template it directly.

O9_family: CWE-79 stored/DOM XSS via unescaped markdown metadata interpolated into HTML templates (escaping missing on the render path, bypassing the token-level XSS filter)

O10_build.toolchain: Node + npm/yarn, Vite build (scripts/build.ts); markdown-it 14, highlight.js, xss
O10_build.project_tests: None: no *.test/*.spec files in the pinned tree and no test script in package.json. Hidden tests would need to call the markdown-it pipeline/plugins directly (node + jsdom for useCopyCode).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Escape (or quote) only the class="language-${language}" interpolation in the highlight callback, or add 'fence' tokens to XSSPlugin, leaving the copy-tip, editorId and click-time innerHTML sites open.

out_of_scope_notes: markdown-it is created with html:true and the default sanitize is the identity (packages/MdEditor/props.ts:140-143), so raw HTML passes unless the integrator configures sanitize or XSSPlugin; this is a design choice, not part of this advisory.
useMermaid writes sanitizeMermaid output via innerHTML (packages/MdEditor/layouts/Content/composition/useMermaid.ts:157), and its default is also the identity; not pursued.
